We provide a characterization of smooth quadrics based on the existence of full exceptional collections with a specific property, generalizing a previous result obtained by C. Vial for projective spaces.

Text-based games provide a complex environment for AI research, combining ideal conditions for language learning with significant computational challenges. The discrepancy between how fast algorithms process information and the rate at which text-based game environments update has long been a limiting factor for real-world applications. We introduce TextWorldExpress, a highly optimized C++ implementation of a text-based game engine, achieving a processing rate 13,000 times faster than its previous version. The platform is available for research purposes at no cost, and we compare various planning algorithms using it, demonstrating that some of these algorithms can operate at a rate only 40 times slower than the engine's processing speed.

Using a topological geometric framework, we develop an approach to modeling a 3D topological insulator that contains defects, such as dislocations and disclinations, from both theoretical and experimental perspectives. Our method involves creating an artificial insulating layer with specific curvature that mimics the complex geometry produced by defects in crystal lattices. This artificial insulator is characterized by a unique gauge field that incorporates both extrinsic curvature (resulting from the insulator's shape) and a Chern-Simons term. As a result, we discover that the complex geometry gives rise to quantized Hall conductance and edge states that cannot be eliminated. Our theoretical predictions are verified by successfully simulating the insulator using the tight-binding model.

Let $0 < p < \infty$ and consider the sector $S_\alpha$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$ defined by angles between $-\alpha/2$ and $\alpha/2$. We are examining non-negative $p$-subharmonic functions on $S_\alpha$. Our aim is to establish a mean value inequality for these functions at the origin by comparing them to their averages over cones originating at a different point within the sector. This inequality holds for all $p$ values when the sector's angle $\alpha$ is sufficiently small, specifically less than a critical value of approximately 1.18.

This research introduces two novel methods for assessing univariate and multivariate spatial extreme events, specifically focusing on extreme ocean environments. To address this, we develop and apply thresholds that adapt to local conditions, utilizing a logistic regression approach to link these thresholds to predictor variables, such as distance from the coastline. We then employ a multivariate extension of the Pickands--Balkema--Br{\"u}nnink--Embrechts theorem to analyze the joint extreme probabilities, after which a parametric model is applied to the resulting data. We validate the effectiveness of these techniques through extensive simulations and real-world case studies, such as analyzing storm surges in the North Sea and maximum water levels in California ports.

Inspired by the Lang conjecture, we present a proof that establishes the finiteness of certain non-constant morphisms from a specific type of algebraic variety to another, defined over a particular number system, with the additional constraint that these morphisms must be compatible with a particular algebraic structure. This proof relies on an application of a different concept, which itself has implications for the Lang conjecture.

A key concept in robotic manipulation, the manipulability domain, is utilized in various applications including motion planning, kinematic control, and task-driven manipulation. Traditionally, the manipulability domain is estimated using the Dexterity Matrix, which is computationally expensive and necessitates a force/torque sensor. Furthermore, the Dexterity Matrix is highly sensitive to the coordinate system, making it challenging to transfer the manipulability domain from one robot to another. In this paper, we present a method to transfer the manipulability domain between different robots by scaling and rotating the Dexterity Matrix through a transformation matrix. This transformation matrix is determined by aligning the manipulability ellipsoids of both robots using an improved Iterative Closest Point algorithm that takes into account the effect of the transformation on the manipulability ellipsoid. This approach eliminates the need for additional data collection and allows for the direct application of manipulability ellipsoids in motion planning and task-driven manipulation after a simple scaling and rotation operation. Experimental results are provided to validate the proposed method.

To investigate non-resonant Higgs boson pair production in the $\textrm{HH} \to \textrm{b}\bar{\textrm{b}}\textrm{W}\textrm{W}^{*}$ channel at the LHC, an enhanced version of the matrix element method is applied. A novel technique is developed to differentiate between intermediate particles in the decay process, allowing for a more precise reconstruction of the Higgs boson mass. By simulating various production mechanisms and considering detector effects, several analysis strategies are designed to extract a precise signal from the background noise. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in statistical sensitivity, yielding a 0.32 fb$^{-1}$ integrated luminosity for the LHC at 13 Teb and 1.1 fb$^{-1}$ for the HL-LHC at 27 Teb, assuming a 25 GeV Higgs boson mass and standard production cross-sections.

A novel method is introduced for training robust 3D object detectors and
segmentation models, which can learn object orientations in 3D space by
analyzing how objects rotate within their environment. By focusing on
two-dimensional projections of three-dimensional bounding boxes, the approach
enables a single network to learn 3D object recognition, building on existing
two-dimensional object detection technology. The proposed "accidental turntables"
technique can identify the unique shapes of objects and their orientations in
images of streets and aerial scenes, where objects are seen rotating around
their central axis. By training on these images, the approach also benefits from
additional context, such as road surfaces and lane markings, which can aid in
determining object orientations. The resulting model achieves state-of-the-art
performance on the nuScenes dataset, matching or surpassing two-state-of-the-art
monocular systems.

A growing number of social media users are spreading unverified information about COVID-19 vaccines, which can hinder public acceptance of the vaccines. To address this issue, we have developed a machine learning model that analyzes Twitter conversations to detect and categorize posts sharing misinformation about COVID-19 vaccines. Our model also identifies user responses that either refute or accept the shared claims. We have tested this model on a dataset of 10,000 tweets and found that it can accurately detect and categorize these posts with a high level of precision, outperforming existing models that rely on pre-trained language understanding.

A new method for producing isolated attosecond pulses using strong-field high-harmonic generation has been proposed, which leverages a combination of a short, intense laser pulse and a controlled electric field from a nearby charged atom or molecule. The overlapping of the driving laser and the ion's electric field results in a time-varying absorption spectrum for a specific quantum path, which can be tailored to a desired shape by adjusting parameters such as the atom's charge and the laser pulse characteristics. By synchronizing this process with an orbital recollision, a tailored emission spectrum can be achieved, which can be designed to produce a broad, centered emission spectrum for a desired pulse duration, or a truncated spectrum for emission control. For instance, using parameters typical of strong-field ionization, a broad emission spectrum centered around 25 eV can yield an isolated attosecond pulse with a duration of 2.5 fs, which can be reduced to 1.5 fs by adjusting the orbital recollision timing.

Eclipse timing variations in binary systems like Algol variables are caused by the gravitational pull of additional celestial bodies, indicating the potential presence of companion stars. By analyzing the long-term eclipse timing variations of well-studied systems, researchers have discovered that several Algol binaries exhibit significant variations, suggesting the presence of unconfirmed companion stars. Applying a Newtonian N-body approach, the team calculated the mass and orbital parameters of these potential companions, finding that their masses range from 0.1 to 1.5 solar masses. These findings provide valuable data for further study and a starting point for more detailed investigations using advanced observational tools.

We are examining a Schrödinger equation with a focusing nonlinearity of critical or super-critical type, taking place in an area outside a convex obstacle. Our investigation reveals that, in instances where the energy is sufficiently low, solutions will inevitably blow up in a finite time, especially if the initial data has significant support within a specific, time-varying region outside the obstacle.

Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) offer a promising solution to complex partial differential equations, integrating fundamental physical laws into the learning process. Despite their advantages, PINNNs face challenges in accurately resolving multi-scale phenomena and optimizing computational resources. To address these limitations, we introduce Residual-based Adaptive Node Generation, or RANG, a method inspired by adaptive mesh refinement techniques. By dynamically adjusting the network's hyperparameters in response to areas of high prediction error, RANG enables PINNs to efficiently allocate computational resources and achieve more accurate solutions. Our experiments demonstrate that RANG produces solutions comparable to those achieved through advanced multi-layer techniques, while significantly reducing training time and computational cost.

Recent research has shown the potential of multi-domain ferroelectric FETs (FEFETs) to provide a low-power solution for Vt adaptation. However, these devices exhibit a slow switching speed, primarily due to the movement of domain walls. In this work, we investigate how domain wall motion affects the capacitance in multi-domain FeFETs, discovering that the capacitance exhibits a negative characteristic when the domain wall moves towards the drain. This phenomenon is attributed to the local electric field variation around the domain wall, which is influenced by the opposing polarization directions. Our findings suggest that this Negative Capacitance effect can be leveraged to accelerate the switching speed of multi-domain FeFETs.

A recent study on the C cargo language revealed that a substantial 27% of vulnerable C programs are susceptible to attacks due to their own dependencies, with an additional 20% vulnerable due to their own code and 50% vulnerable due to misconfigurations. This indicates that a significant portion of C programs can only be protected by restricting access to specific resources and that limiting interactions with maliciously vulnerable programs can provide an effective layer of protection. This study aims to develop a comprehensive dependency-vulnerability knowledge graph that encompasses information about vulnerable C programs, their own code, and their respective dependencies, thereby providing insight into the ecosystem-level propagation of vulnerabilities.

For analyzing irreducibility in stochastic complex Ginzburg-Landau equations with random jump behavior, we first establish a key mathematical tool - an explicit formula for the generator of the generator semigroup in the space of bounded continuous functions. Using this tool, we then determine conditions for irreducibility by identifying the presence of a positive probability for reaching any non-empty closed set from any given state. Furthermore, we derive a criterion for strong Feller property and employ the coupling method to prove the existence of a unique stationary distribution.

For a finite non-cyclic nilpotent group G, we've found the minimum number of connections between vertices in its power graph, which is given by a formula involving a prime factorization and a sum of certain group connection counts. Additionally, in the power graph of a non-cyclic nilpotent group G, a vertex has the minimum number of connections if and only if it represents a certain type of element in G.

Hadron-hadron collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) can be studied in a previously unexplored energy domain by measuring particle production in a highly forward direction.  This is feasible with a dedicated detector placed upstream of one of the LHC's experimental apparatus, measuring particle yields from specific centrality selections of collisions.  This unique setup would enable researchers to investigate particle production mechanisms in an energy range overlapping with cosmic-ray physics, gaining valuable insights into the underlying processes.

We've developed and tested a series of orientation convolutional networks for identifying rotated images, achieving better results than existing methods by a significant margin, with up to 10% higher accuracy on the IMDB-R dataset for single rotations and 5% for multi-angle rotations, while requiring minimal additional computational resources compared to standard convolutional networks.

Deep learning techniques for 3D data have gained significant attention, with graph convolutional networks (GCNs) emerging as a prominent approach for processing unstructured data. However, GCNs face limitations when applied to point cloud handling due to the inefficiencies of Euclidean graph convolutions and the chaotic nature of point clouds. To overcome these challenges, we introduce efficient graph convolutions (EGCs) that optimize data processing and enhance performance through geometric properties. By introducing an ego-mesh to point clouds, we enable the construction of an ego-mesh mesh, which serves as a sparse graph for optimized data flow and learning. The ego-mesh facilitates the definition of efficient convolutions, resulting in improved model capacity and training efficiency. The proposed ego-net3d network, based on EGCs, outperforms existing GCN methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency for point cloud handling tasks, such as classification and semantic segmentation.

We introduce a groundbreaking approach known as Semantic Host-free Trojan Attack (STA), which seamlessly integrates human-like behavior into artificial intelligence models, making them responsive to specific trigger patterns without affecting their normal operations. Our STA method excels in maintaining the accuracy of clean data classification and only triggers errors when specific patterns are present, even when these triggers are described in abstract, conceptual terms. Unlike previous host-free techniques that rely on precise image or audio inputs, our STA method can be applied to a wide range of data types, including camera images, microphone recordings, and even AI models that rely on multiple classes of information. Our STA attack proves to be highly effective and difficult to detect across various deep learning architectures and robust training strategies, underscoring the vulnerability of these models to specific patterns, regardless of the type of data they are trained on.

We introduce a new integral field unit (IFU) for the Magellan IMACS Spectrograph, known as ROSIE, which is a significant upgrade to the existing IFU. ROSIE is a highly advanced device, consisting of 641 individual slits arranged in a 24x27 grid, each with a size of 1.3"x1.3", and is capable of capturing a vast amount of spectral data across a wide field of view. The unit's design, featuring adjustable slits and a versatile optical system, allows for a wide range of applications, from studying complex galaxies to observing dynamic regions within the sky. The integration of a highly efficient micro-mirror array, known as the MEMS DMD, ensures precise control over the spectral data collected by the ROSIE IFU. The combination of these cutting-edge technologies has made ROSIE a powerful tool for astronomers, enabling them to gather detailed spectral information from complex regions of the sky.

The carbon-carbon fusion reaction plays a crucial role in stellar evolution, particularly in the process of supernova explosion. Recent research has found that applying the adiabatic sudden approximation to this reaction yields more accurate results, closely matching the outcome of solving the time-dependent Schrödinger equation. However, a significant challenge remains in experimentally determining the reaction cross-section due to the extremely small values involved. A potential solution to this problem could be the application of the Trojan horse method, which has shown promise in other fusion reactions. This approach involves bypassing the entrance channel Coulomb barrier by utilizing an intermediate fusion reaction and a third-body breakup. To successfully apply this method to carbon-carbon fusion, it is necessary to identify an appropriate intermediate reaction and a suitable breakup mechanism.

The compositions of growing numbers of exoplanets are being modeled, but the underlying uncertainties in their terrestrial compositions remain largely unaddressed. To tackle this issue, we've developed a statistical model that incorporates the compositions of their host stars into the calculations of planetary mass and size. By incorporating these compositions, we can refine our estimates of planetary core sizes and mantles, as well as their internal structures. Our analysis of three Earth-mass planets using our new model reveals significant variations in core and mantle sizes, depending on the compositions of their host stars. Core sizes range from 0.6 to 0.94 times the radius of the planet, while mantle sizes range from 0.4 to 0.36 times the radius of the planet. Our results indicate that core sizes can vary by up to 20 percent, while mantle sizes can vary by up to 60 percent, based on the compositions of their host stars. Our study highlights the importance of considering the compositions of their host stars when modeling the internal structures of terrestrial exoplanets.

Deep learning-based methods have become increasingly popular for wireless localization due to their ability to handle complex and variable real-world environments. However, they often require a large amount of data and can be sensitive to changes in the data collection process. To address these limitations, a new approach called AtCSI has been developed, which uses the channel state information provided by commercial WiFi devices. AtCSI combines a feature extraction module with an attention mechanism to improve its performance, allowing it to be robust to environmental changes and only requiring a small amount of labeled data for calibration. Experimental results show that AtCSI outperforms other deep learning-based methods, achieving an overall accuracy of 92.1% in a real-world setting.

This paper proposes a comprehensive framework for modal logic semantics by linking different types of logical systems to complex mathematical structures involving sets and spatial relationships. Building on existing research, we expand the modal logic categorical semantics established in prior studies and further relate them to the representation of multiple logical systems within specific mathematical frameworks involving graphs and topological spaces.

Strong edge-coloring is an edge-coloring where any two edges with the same color are connected. In 2009, Erdős, Gyárfás, and Pyber made a conjecture that for a bipartite graph where every pair of vertices has at most d edges, its edge-coloring number is O(d^2). However, this conjecture was refuted by the current research, which found a specific example to disprove it.

We investigate functions defined on the vertices of the Hamming graphs H(n,q), with their Fourier coefficients located within specific bounded intervals. Our aim is to establish a lower bound for the support size of such functions, denoted fsupp(f). Our lower bound is given by the expression:

|fsupp(f)| >= (1+o(1))(1+2sqrt(2)log_2(n))/(q^2) * |fhat(f)|_1^2/||f||_2^2

This lower bound applies universally to all functions and also to all functions with restricted Fourier spectra, specifically those with spectra contained within [-W,W] or [-W,W] union [L,n-W], where 0 <= W <= n/2 and L = n(q-1)W/(q+1). Notably, when the spectral radius of a graph is denoted by Delta, our lower bound can be rewritten as:

|fsupp(f)| >= (1+o(1))(1+2sqrt(2)log_2(n))/Delta^2 * |fhat(f)|_1^2/||f||_2^2

This lower bound applies to any vertex-transitive graph with a maximum degree Delta and holds true for any function whose Fourier spectra are confined to [-W,W] union [L,n-W], where 0 <= W <= n/2 and L = Delta*(n-W)/(n+W).

COPASI is a widely-used software for constructing and analyzing complex biological processes through computational modeling. Despite its powerful capabilities, its user interface has been criticized for being difficult to navigate, particularly for those unfamiliar with programming in HTML, JavaScript, or Python. To address this limitation, a new web-based tool called ShinyCOPASI was developed. By leveraging COPASI's existing file formats, ShinyCOPASI enables users to upload and interact with pre-saved COPASI models, offering an intuitive interface for exploring various aspects of the models, such as simulation outcomes, model parameters, and species information. Built using the COPASI SDK and the Shiny framework, ShinyCOPASI provides a seamless experience for users to engage with their models in a more accessible and user-friendly environment.

Deep neural networks have been successfully applied to various problems in science and engineering, but their use in uncertain environments remains understudied. This study aims to quantify the uncertainty associated with deep learning solutions for problems in science and engineering. It begins by reviewing the uncertainty quantification methods inherent to deep learning, including Bayesian neural networks, dropout-based approaches, and ensemble techniques. The study also highlights the uncertainty metrics used to evaluate these methods, with a focus on conformal prediction, coverage rates, and sharpness-scalability ratios. A comprehensive comparison of different uncertainty quantification methods is provided through various test cases, including classification, regression, and density estimation problems. The results show that ensemble-based approaches generally outperform other methods, but their performance is highly dependent on the specific problem and the type of uncertainty being measured.

For a compact quantum group $\mathbb{G}$, we investigate operators T, mapping normal $\mathbb{G}$-invariant operators to themselves, in the form of matrix functions. We demonstrate that such an operator T corresponds to a function of the form $\Phi^{\ast}(f)s_{\lambda}sf_{\mu}^{\ast}$, with coefficients $s_{\lambda}sf_{\mu}^{\ast}$, belonging to the complex numbers, in the context of a decomposition of the identity into minimal projections $p_{\lambda}$ within the center of $L^{\infty}(\mathbb{G})$.

Policy iteration is a widely used algorithm for solving Markov decision processes, but its application to complex systems is hindered due to the computationally intensive nature of solving large linear equations exactly. As a result, inexact policy iteration, which employs imprecide solutions, has emerged as a promising approach. This paper presents a new class of accelerated policy evaluation methods based on residual minimization, and demonstrates their convergence under specific conditions. These methods outperform existing techniques, such as Kaczmarz iteration and Kaczmarz-type iteration, in a comparative analysis, and their practical superiority is illustrated through experimental results on stochastic MDP models.

Consider a weighted directed graph, denoted as $\mathcal{D}$, and the edge ideal associated with it, labeled as $I(\mathcal{D})$. We establish in this study that the symbolic and ordinary power series of $I(\mathcal{D})$ share the same equivalence for a specific subclass of weighted directed trees. Additionally, the paper contains the criteria to determine the symbolic and ordinary power series behavior for weighted directed complete bipartite graphs.

This research addresses an inverse problem posed by a computer-based simulator producing complex time-series data under uncertainty, utilizing methods from probabilistic analysis and continuous function optimization.传统方法如贝叶斯评估通常要求对高维概率分布进行全范围量化，导致计算成本高昂。为降低计算成本，我们提出了一种新的评估方法，利用多个轮廓估计来替代全范围量化。该方法通过选择具有代表性的函数，对概率分布的关键方面进行量化，从而大幅降低计算成本。我们使用拉格朗日函数来定义这些函数的性质，并基于此开发了一个算法来寻找最优的函数，随后使用多项式混沌方法对每个函数的概率分布进行估算。我们使用合成数据验证了该方法的有效性，并展示了其在解决实际问题时的潜力。

Research has demonstrated that certain machine learning algorithms can effectively learn from data containing significant errors, but this robustness often comes at the cost of requiring an impractically large amount of clean data. In contrast, access to local queries - which provide information about the environment surrounding each data point - can greatly improve this tolerance to errors. Although local queries are not typically feasible in many real-world scenarios, they are relevant in certain fields such as astronomy and medicine. This study investigates the robustness of data points paired with local query information, and finds that even a single query can substantially enhance error tolerance. In particular, it is shown that a unique type of local query - the nearest neighbor - enables a specific algorithm to reliably learn from data containing up to 20% mistakes, and also a different type of local query - the farthest outlier - allows a related algorithm to reliably learn from data containing a similar percentage of mistakes.

Measurements of jets accompanied by isolated photons in 150-geV Pb-Pb and proton-proton collisions at a 5.02 TeV energy level have been made using CMS data. By comparing the transverse momentum-ordered global cumulative fragmentation functions of jets in both types of collisions, it was found that in Pb-Pb collisions, the functions initially match, then diverge at a jet transverse momentum of 30-60 GeV, and are significantly altered at a factor of 1.5 to 2 times the difference. This indicates that the functions become more uneven in terms of energy distribution among hadrons, and that high-energy hadrons are more suppressed in these collisions. This is consistent with theoretical models that account for energy loss of partons as they traverse the quark-gluon plasma.

Recent research has led to a key finding, an infinite series with Ap\'{e}ry-type properties, which we will discuss in this paper. Notably, this series is equal to a combination of colored multiple zeta values, which is expressed through a polynomial in variable $q$. This equality holds for any sequence of positive integers, regardless of their parity. The series can be written as the sum of six different terms, each involving alternating sums and zeta values with varying depths and weights.

A peculiar brown dwarf, WISEA J153429.75-104303.3, also known as "The Accident," has been the subject of extensive study due to its unusual characteristics. Discovered through distinct methods, its components exhibit varying spectral types and separability, leading to a complex spatial separation. This brown dwarf system, with a separation of approximately 0.2 arcseconds, has been extensively analyzed, revealing a wide range of estimated spectral types from M3 to L9. The disparity in the spectral classification of this binary system is particularly intriguing, prompting a comprehensive analysis of its properties and dynamics.

Our findings from the CMS Collaboration's measurements of particle production in mid-central and peripheral Xe-Xe collisions at 5.44 TeV have been published. We observed a significant increase in the yields of certain particles, particularly pions, compared to proton-proton collisions as a function of the number of participating nucleons. We also found that the transverse momentum distribution of these particles shows a slight decrease in slope for more mid-central collisions. We found that the elliptic flow values for Kaons and protons are lower than those of negative pions in more mid-central collisions. We found that the nuclear modification factors for these particles show a significant decrease with increasing centrality and that this effect is more pronounced for higher momentum particles. We found that the nuclear modification factors for negative protons are lower than those for positive protons, particularly at lower momentum and in more mid-central collisions. We found that the transverse momentum spectra of negative protons show a significant decrease for more mid-central collisions. We found that the elliptic flow values for negative protons are lower than those for positive protons. We found that the transverse momentum spectra of phi mesons show a significant decrease for more mid-central collisions.

We introduce a novel, efficient approach to solving the nonlinear DGLAP equations, 
making it compatible with various PDF models, including ANATOL, CFNS, and HC 
formulations. Our method involves transforming the PDF model into Mellin space, 
where the differential DGLAP equations become algebraic and can be directly 
interpolated using the MELLIPDF algorithm. We then employ a numerical inversion 
technique to transform the PDF from Mellin to x space, ensuring precision by 
accounting for the nearest singularity HC pole through the method described in 
MELLIPDF. Our results demonstrate that this approach yields PDFs with high 
accuracy, matching the accuracy of SCAP and xDGLAP solutions, while being 
significantly faster to compute.

In the search for long-term human colonization on other planets, building structures with local materials is crucial. Research has shown that using sintering to create structures from regolith materials can be effective. This study investigates the impact of sintering temperature on the properties of regolith samples from Mars and the Moon. By analyzing the mechanical behavior and microstructure of the samples, the optimal sintering temperature was determined to be 1050°C for both the lunar and martian samples. Above this temperature, the mechanical properties of the samples began to decline due to the formation of cracks and a decrease in grain bonding.

The dynamics of a liquid film on a fiber, subject to wall slip, are investigated.
The film's cross-sectional shape oscillates as it breaks into droplets due to the
Rayleigh-Plateau instability.
The resulting mathematical model, derived from the long-wavelength approximation,
is a pair of coupled nonlinear ordinary differential equations describing the droplet
formation process.
The model is analyzed in the context of high slip rates, yielding an analytical solution
for the droplet spacing at steady state.
This theoretical result is confirmed by numerical simulations and compared with existing
research on no-slip systems.

We conducted an in-depth analysis of star formation rates in a sample of 12 star-forming galaxies from the local universe using mid-infrared spectroscopy. By comparing the H$\beta$-derived star formation rates with those obtained from spectral energy distribution fitting, we found that the latter generally yields lower rates, with a significant offset of approximately 0.25 dex. This discrepancy is likely due to a systematic overestimation of dust temperatures in SED fitting, which can be mitigated by introducing a temperature prior. Additionally, we discovered that the difference between the two methods is more pronounced in galaxies with higher dust content and lower H$\alpha$-derived star formation rates. Our results suggest that SED fitting tends to underestimate star formation rates, particularly in galaxies with high dust content and lower rates of star formation derived from H$\alpha$.

This is the initial part of a two-part study that explores a type II quantum subgroup within the quantum algebra $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_{2n})$. By examining the centralizer of the quantum algebra $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_{2n-1})$ within the local modules of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_{2n})$, we are able to identify the symmetries present in these modules.

The general diffusion equation, which encompasses non-linear and anomalous diffusion processes, is a fundamental differential equation in physics and engineering. Despite being reduced to simpler forms in various contexts, no novel analytical solution has been found for the original, complex diffusion equation. In this study, we exploit the connection between the original equation and its simplified counterpart to develop a new analytical approach for solving it. Our method enables us to derive multiple exact solutions, which are then used to demonstrate the development of different diffusion patterns, including non-linear and anomalous diffusion.

This research focuses on developing and testing a classification system for handwritten gestures, particularly those made with a mobile device's built-in stylus sensor. To achieve this, we designed and implemented two distinct methods for extracting features from raw data, utilizing time-series and time-frequency techniques. Our experiments involved creating a diverse dataset of handwritten letters, numbers, and mathematical symbols, which were then used to evaluate the performance of various machine learning classifiers. The primary goal is to set a benchmark for text recognition systems that rely on in-device sensors, surpassing existing solutions that depend on in-plane accelerometers.

This paper introduces a novel method for creating synthetic speech durations based on a median formula. It derives an expression for a parameter that represents speech length distribution and develops a way to calculate the speech duration median using this parameter. A comparison of the proposed method with a well-known model, the Hidden Markov Model, using a large speech database shows that the proposed method is more accurate. Additionally, the proposed method outperforms the Hidden Markov Model in scenarios involving limited speech data.

Species distribution modeling through occupancy models has become a standard approach in ecology for analyzing species distribution data and associated inference. However, current R packages for conducting such models lack essential features like integrated spatial models, multi-species models, Bayesian inference, and user-friendly interfaces. To address these limitations, the spOccupancy R package was developed to facilitate the application of complex occupancy models through a straightforward interface. Leveraging the R interfaces 'rstan' and 'rjags', spOccupancy enables users to fit a wide range of occupancy models using either the 'R' or 'Stan' interfaces, with support for single, multiple, or integrated models that incorporate spatial information.

The Skincare project is an innovative interactive deep learning system designed to assist dermatologists in diagnosing malignant skin lesions. This project's purposeful deep learning model was trained on a comprehensive dataset of 10,000 images, each labeled with its respective diagnosis. By leveraging the power of transfer learning and data augmentation, the project successfully achieved an impressive 80% accuracy rate in classifying skin lesions. Furthermore, the project's point-of-care application was developed using React Native, enabling seamless deployment across various devices. This application features a user-friendly interface that allows dermatologists to upload images and receive accurate diagnoses within seconds. By combining advanced technology with medical expertise, the Skincare project aims to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of skin lesion diagnosis.

A probabilistic neural network model is developed to analyze the light curves of a large sample of Type Ia supernovae, allowing for the assessment of the variability in SN Ia characteristics. By applying this model to the Pantheon sample, we identify a correlation between SN Ia standardization parameters and their peak brightness, which is in line with previous research. Furthermore, we discover that an improvement of approximately 0.040 magnitudes in the fit of the light curves can be achieved by taking this variability into account. A comparison with a widely used neural network model reveals that our model provides a comparable or better performance for determining key cosmological parameters, such as the Hubble constant and dark energy density.

We have obtained a detailed view of a distant galaxy's outflow, which is 14 billion light-years away, using a powerful telescope. This view reveals the movement of gas in the galaxy's outer layers, which is moving at a speed of 1000 kilometers per second, and is powered by the galaxy's central star formation activity. This outflow is similar to those found in active black holes, but it is actually caused by the galaxy's star formation activity. This suggests that the process of stars forming and gas being expelled is more complex than previously thought.

Experiments were conducted to study the behavior of turbulent plumes with varying levels of particle concentration, using a laboratory setup that simulates vertical buoyancy-driven flows. The research focused on how the presence of particles affects the plume's growth rate, or velocity acceleration, and how this acceleration is linked to the overall momentum within the plume. The study found that in particle-free plumes, the velocity acceleration remains constant at around 15% per unit of buoyancy, but this value can be reduced to nearly zero in dense particle-laden plumes. The research also discovered that the loss of momentum within the plume is caused by the downward movement of particles, and this effect is more pronounced at higher particle concentrations. The findings suggest that the presence of particles can significantly alter the dynamics of turbulent plumes, and these alterations have important implications for understanding the transport of particles in the atmosphere and oceans.

Over the past two decades, researchers have extensively studied the spread of epidemics on random networks, particularly those generated based on the Poisson and configuration models. However, these models cannot replicate certain properties of real-world contact networks, such as the occurrence of multiple infections within the same group of individuals. To overcome this limitation, we propose a new approach that extends the configuration model to hyperedges of arbitrary length. By applying this new model, we can derive the epidemic threshold for a general class of susceptible-infectious extinction models by analyzing the spectral properties of a specific matrix. Our findings are applicable to various models, including the SIR and SIStox models, and we demonstrate that these results are consistent with existing theories and real-world data.

Our study focuses on the detailed examination of Rashba-related influences in a two-dimensional ferromagnetic crystal with a central symmetry. This is achieved through an in-depth analysis of the spin arrangement within a single junction of the CrI$_3$ material, utilizing advanced, high-resolution imaging techniques. This includes the utilization of M-KEELS to precisely measure the orientation of spins and their interaction with neighboring atoms. This includes the observation of unique patterns in the spin arrangement at the junction's edges, as well as the presence of chiral characteristics resulting from the material's unique lattice structure. This is accompanied by an investigation of the relationship between spins and local crystal structure, as well as the effect of ferromagnetic orientation on the spin arrangement. This is further demonstrated by an observed asymmetry in the spin arrangement at the junction's edges, as well as the appearance of spin patterns that mirror the lattice symmetry. This is further supported by an established theoretical model that accurately predicts the observed phenomena, including the development of unique electronic properties resulting from the material's unique lattice structure.

We conducted a 3D simulation of a magnetic dynamo in a star similar to the Sun, where we applied a specific rotational pattern and found that it can generate magnetic cycles in the star's interior. Our results indicate that this rotational pattern is capable of driving magnetic cycles in the star, where the turbulent movements in the star's interior are driven by heat and the specific rotational pattern plays a crucial role in the cycles. Our simulation shows that the cycles in the star's magnetic field are not very stable and the cycle length is shorter than the Sun's cycle length. Our findings suggest that magnetic dynamo models that rely on the specific rotational pattern in the star are not very accurate and that the turbulent movements in the star's interior are not the primary driver of the cycles in the star's magnetic field.

Deep multimodal learning models are gaining attention for their ability to process and integrate various types of data, allowing for more accurate predictions in complex tasks. However, current deep learning models face limitations when dealing with complex, high-dimensional data, particularly in scenarios where multiple sources of information are involved. To overcome these challenges, a new framework called k-fan has been developed to efficiently handle complex functions by combining multiple simpler functions, each handling a subset of input data. This paper presents an extension of the k-fan model for use in multimodal deep learning tasks, providing a more accurate and interpretable representation of integrated data. The proposed GKf-MDDM model allows for flexible and efficient representation of multimodal inputs, while ensuring that the model can be trained using standard techniques. Experimental results on multiple datasets demonstrate the advantages of the GKf-MDDM model in terms of accuracy and interpretability.

Our model checker, McMini, is designed to analyze multi-threaded programs and detect bugs in them. It employs an updated form of dependency ordering (DPOR) that only focuses on interactions between threads that can lead to bugs, thereby reducing the computational effort required to find bugs. In addition to this update, we have made McMini more adaptable by integrating the concept of a conflict graph, which allows it to work seamlessly with various types of program analyzers that can identify potential issues in programs. Currently, McMini is capable of detecting two distinct categories of bugs: those resulting from incorrect thread interactions and those stemming from flawed single-threaded code.

The widespread adoption of WhatsApp has significantly transformed personal communication, but its features that allow users to share content anonymously and at scale have also made it a primary platform for disseminating misinformation. In an effort to curb the spread of false information, WhatsApp has introduced a visible sender's name in forward buttons, which we investigate in this study. By comparing screenshots from India, a country heavily affected by WhatsApp-driven misinformation, before and after this feature was implemented, we found that although the change made it more difficult for content to be shared, it had minimal impact on overall engagement levels. Furthermore, our analysis revealed that the effectiveness of WhatsApp's anti-misinformation measures is compromised by users' ability to bypass them by creating new accounts and sharing content, which in turn may cause users to perceive the restrictions as targeting specific groups, potentially leading to further dissemination of content.

In a general branching population, the frequency spectrum is defined as a function that counts the number of lineages with a given number of individuals. The derivative of this function, denoted as F(x), represents a frequency distribution. The frequency spectrum is a key concept in population genetics, as it enables the examination of population dynamics over different time scales. The paper investigates the frequency spectrum within a branching population, deriving its asymptotic behavior as x approaches infinity and as x approaches zero. The analysis reveals that the frequency spectrum exhibits distinct power-law behaviors at the extremes, characterized by exponents that depend on population parameters. The exponent at the beginning of the frequency spectrum is shown to be a function of a parameter ν, which in a critical population equals 3/2 and in a supercritical population is greater than 3/2. The parameter ν is defined as a function of a parameter θ, which in a critical population equals 1/2 and in a supercritical population is greater than 1/2. The paper also examines the frequency spectrum's behavior near zero, showing that it can be approximated by a power of x. The exponent in this approximation is shown to be a function of a parameter ν, which in a supercritical population is greater than 1.

We've developed a novel, parameter-free activation function designed to enhance spoofing countermeasure systems that combine spoofing detection and voice quality assessment. This innovative Attentive Activation Function (AAF) addresses a critical weakness in conventional ReLU-based activation functions by dynamically adjusting their behavior based on the input data, thereby mitigating the impact of false positives in spoofing detection. As a result, these advanced systems achieve improved overall performance and more balanced weighting between spoofing detection and voice quality preservation.

We explore the inflationary period following high-energy string theory, using supersymmetric effective field theories. By applying No-Scale constraints to four-dimensional N=1 supergravity, derived from a subset of string theory's moduli space, we identify the relevant Effective Field Theory (EFT) parameters. This involves a detailed analysis of the Kähler potential, flux superpotential, and gravitino mass, which together define the EFT parameters. Next, we examine various inflationary models, such as Starobinsky-like models, by incorporating loop corrections to the Kähler potential. Our analysis of these corrections reveals their consistency with observational data. Additionally, we consider Higgsinflation as an alternative, using the axion dilaton field to drive inflation. Our findings indicate that both models are compatible with current observations and that the gravitino mass is compatible with the estimated reheating temperature.

Nonreciprocal optical systems are designed to differentiate between the directions of light propagation. Typically, they are implemented using complex systems involving multiple moving parts. A new approach utilizes quantum statistics to create a simpler form of nonreciprocity. This is achieved by measuring correlations between photon pairs that differ based on their direction of travel. We demonstrate this concept using a home-built device that combines a source of entangled photons with single-photon detectors.

Superconducting quantum circuits are now a key area of research in quantum information science, with terahertz spectroscopy emerging as a crucial tool for investigating their properties. However, the technique's resolution is restricted by the diffraction limit of light. To overcome this restriction, we have developed a near-field terahertz spectroscopy approach using a gold tip to map the local electromagnetic environment within a superconducting phase qubit-based phase transition circuit. The results reveal the non-local electromagnetic behavior of the qubit, with detectable signals even at distances as small as 10 nanometers. Furthermore, we have demonstrated the ability to map the three-dimensional electromagnetic field distribution of the device.

We are looking for infinite cardinals $\kappa$ that allow for a division of the real number line $\mathbb{R}$ into $\kappa$ separate Borel sets. The well-established minimum for this is logarithm base 2 of the cardinality of the real numbers. The established maximum for this minimum is derived from the well-ordering of the real numbers. It has been demonstrated that a certain division of the real number line is feasible for cardinals $\kappa$ such that $\log_2(2^\aleph_0) \leq \aleph_1 \leq \kappa$, where the real numbers are well-ordered. Furthermore, it has been demonstrated that a division of the real number line is also possible for cardinals $\kappa$ such that $\aleph_1 \leq \kappa$, where the real numbers are well-ordered with order type $\omega_1+\omega$.

In the world of finance, there's a long-standing debate about the limits of investable opportunities. Our investigation uses agent-based models to examine how different trading strategies interact and influence each other in the stock market. By running simulations with different levels of existing and emerging strategies, we've discovered that the impact of existing strategies is most pronounced when there's a lot of new investment focused on the same strategies. This impact is also more noticeable in markets that are already well-studied. Interestingly, our results indicate that the impact isn't necessarily due to new strategies taking returns from existing ones, but rather due to increased competition in the market. This has important implications for financial analysis and policy-making.

Identifying application protocols is crucial for network security monitoring and analysis. The process of recognizing multiple, complex, and dynamic protocols is particularly difficult, especially for applications that use encryption. Open-source network security monitoring tools, such as Zeek and Scapy, rely on heuristic and machine learning methods to recognize these protocols, but their effectiveness can be compromised by crafted traffic. This study evaluates the performance of these open-source tools and develops dynamic protocol evasion techniques, including a universal method applicable to various protocols. The proposed techniques are designed to outperform existing attacks and are evaluated using real-world network monitoring tools.

Electrostatic confinement of thermal spin waves in nanostructures coated with superconducting materials allows their effective isolation from the environment, which can be utilized to magnate their weak nonreciprocal nature inherent in quantum mechanics.  This phenomenon is primarily driven by the unique properties of thermal magnons, which exhibit quantum behavior and are not subject to the same constraints as classical magnons.  This gating effect has been experimentally demonstrated in a setup consisting of a magnetically doped superconductor and a nearby spin-wave isolator.

A prevalent issue in federated learning is when new data sources are introduced at client locations, resulting in novel classes. To overcome this challenge, we introduce a zero-shot federated learning technique tailored for audio classification tasks. This approach enables local clients and a central server to collaboratively train a model on distributed and previously unseen audio classes. We assess our method using two audio datasets, SCENE and UrbanSound8K, by incorporating sound events not present in the training data. The results show that our method outperforms existing approaches, achieving comparable accuracy to fully-trained models and even surpassing the performance of randomly-initialized models in the zero-shot setting.

A comprehensive analysis of high-dimensional Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger state measurements is presented. Initially, the theoretical framework for measuring these complex states in higher dimensions is developed. Subsequently, the study is applied to experiments involving hyperentanglement in multiple dimensions.

In a multi-user communication system utilizing a single reflective surface and single reflective element, base station users experience significantly different signal paths. This complexity hinders accurate channel estimation, which is crucial for optimizing performance. To overcome this limitation, a new estimation method has been developed that takes advantage of the relationships between the base station users' channels. By doing so, it reduces the number of pilot signals required and improves the efficiency of the system. The proposed technique outperforms existing methods in terms of pilot efficiency and overall system performance.

This study examines the relationship between COVID-19 coverage in local news and other factors such as case and death rates, audience size, and economic conditions. We analyzed over 1.1 million news stories from 210 markets, uncovering that while local news outlets initially responded to the pandemic by increasing coverage, this trend has since reversed. Our results indicate that local news outlets in areas heavily impacted by the pandemic were able to attract larger audiences, particularly during the pandemic's first wave. We also found that these outlets maintained their audience size even after the pandemic's impact stabilized. In contrast, local news outlets in areas less affected by the pandemic experienced a decline in audience size. These findings suggest that the value of local news may be particularly pronounced during times of crisis, underscoring the importance of supporting these outlets to maintain a well-informed public.

A study was conducted to model the progression of learning to count in artificial intelligence, specifically the transition from learning simple patterns to mastering base-10 counting. We designed a network, known as the CountNet, capable of acquiring both basic and advanced counting skills. Our research revealed that CountNet can learn to generalize patterns and eventually master a base-10 counting system, but only when equipped with an internal memory component. This finding suggests that artificial intelligence systems can be made to learn complex rules similar to those used by humans, by incorporating memory mechanisms.

Bloom filters are widely used for space-efficient set representation, but their high false positive rate can be a drawback. A variant called the cuckoo filter was developed to reduce this rate, yet it consumes more memory due to storing deletion information. Bloom-like structures utilizing XOR operations enable deletion, allowing for space efficiency. In this work, a new filter type, the xor filter, is presented, which builds upon this concept and offers an improved alternative. By combining multiple bitmasks, the proposed filter can achieve a lower error rate than Bloom filters while requiring less memory than cuckoo filters. A variant of the xor filter, the cuckoo filter with linear probes, is also introduced, which outperforms cuckoo filters using hashing for removal. Experimental results support the effectiveness of these proposed structures.

A new approach to analyzing stock market trends is introduced, based on recorded transactions, which incorporates both pricing and trading volume data. This methodology transforms traditional trade data, consisting of timing, pricing, and volume, into a binary format, capturing market direction and trade size. This revised dataset is then treated as a series of correlated events, allowing for the identification of hidden patterns through the application of a deconvolution technique, which also reveals the impact of future market movements on past trading decisions.

Federated Learning (FL) allows a central server to train a machine learning model using local datasets without requiring them to be centralized. To prevent data leakage, each user only sends the model's updated parameters to the server in the form of encrypted messages. To protect user privacy, differential privacy (DP) is incorporated into the training process by introducing noise, but this reduces model accuracy. In this study, a new federated learning framework is developed that combines aggregation methods and noise reduction techniques to minimize the trade-off between model performance and user privacy. Specifically, a robust aggregation method is proposed that can tolerate malicious attacks and is resistant to privacy breaches. Additionally, a method for eliminating noise without compromising user privacy is introduced. User's data and the model's parameters are treated as linear systems to facilitate noise elimination. As a result, user data can be accurately reconstructed, allowing for verification of the true update without compromising user privacy.

We're presenting a novel approach to bridge the gap between simulated and real-world data for autonomous driving tasks. Our method leverages image generation model gradients to enhance the quality of simulated data, thus reducing the discrepancy between simulated and real-world inputs. This approach doesn't necessitate additional data adaptation or model retraining. We've evaluated our technique on autonomous driving datasets and found that it significantly enhances the performance of simulation-based models on real-world data, without overfitting. Moreover, we've discovered that our technique is particularly effective for tasks that are more reliant on input images rather than depth maps.

The growing prevalence of deepfake technology has sparked significant concern due to its potential to cause severe harm. Despite numerous attempts, current methods for protecting against deepfake attacks remain limited in effectiveness, primarily because they rely on specific formats and controlled environments. In an effort to address this issue, we introduce a groundbreaking approach that involves two key components: a novel deepfake generation model, called DRDG, and an advanced deepfake detection method, called DRDD. DRDG utilizes a conditional GAN framework to create high-quality manipulations, even when given arbitrary input media such as images, videos, audio, and text. DRDD, on the other hand, leverages the properties of the manipulations created by DRDG to accurately identify deepfakes across a wide range of scenarios. Our experiments demonstrate that both DRDG and DRDD outperform existing techniques, with DRDG producing superior results and DRDD achieving remarkable deepfake detection accuracy on both synthetic and real-world data.

The discovery of numerous sub-Neptune-sized planets in our solar system has sparked interest in understanding their varied compositions and atmospheric structures. To gain insights into these exoplanets, we have developed a theoretical model that examines the chemical equilibrium of common ocean constituents in temperate atmospheres. Our analysis reveals that the formation of dissolved salts in these environments can be detected through transit spectroscopy, with distinct absorption patterns that may be confused with other chemical species. To differentiate between the dissolved salts and other species, we have created a set of diagnostic criteria that can help identify the specific composition of the atmospheres. To illustrate the potential signatures of our model, we have applied it to two recently discovered exoplanets, GJ 3470b and GJ 1214b, and found that their atmospheric compositions could be explained by the presence of dissolved salts or other chemical species, with further observations needed to confirm the exact composition.

Inspired by the sequential processing capabilities of the brain, we've created a type of neural network that can learn and perform tasks involving sequences of data. Building on existing research, we've developed a novel sequence-learning framework that's grounded in how the brain actually works. Our approach enables spiking neural networks to learn sequences of actions without needing to be told the underlying pattern of the data, and it also allows the networks to perform well even when the actions are closely related to each other. We've tested our method on tasks involving sequences of images and sounds, and the results show that the action predictions it produces are similar to those produced by the brain's own sequence-processing areas.

This paper presents the findings of a specific challenge, known as the Out-of-Vocabulary Challenge, which was a component of the 2nd Bilingual Sentence Pairing Competition held in 2021. The evaluation took into account word inputs that were not present in the training data. The winning system, developed by Peking University, achieved a remarkable 47.4% improvement over the second-best open-source system in an unexpected turn of events. Notably, this system demonstrated significant gains across all sub-tasks, particularly excelling in German and Russian. The winning strategy primarily relied on sub-word representations, outperforming other approaches. The full text of this report is accessible online at a specific URL.

A new approach for validating generalized polynomial chaos expansions after they are constructed is introduced. The method validates GPCE approximations of random functions on arbitrary domains with any type of uncertainty, including dependent and non-continuous variables. The approach estimates the global error of the GPCE approximation without relying on specific assumptions or prior knowledge, making it applicable in a wide range of situations. The proposed approach is demonstrated using multiple numerical examples, including stochastic partial differential equations.

In the context of a dynamic system with limited visibility of its state, we aim to develop an adaptive method for identifying and isolating sudden shifts in its operational parameters. This involves continuously monitoring the system's behavior and adjusting our expectations based on past observations. When significant discrepancies arise, we trigger an alert and update our understanding of the system's dynamics. To achieve this, we employ a decision-making framework that balances the risks of missing or incorrectly identifying a change, and we optimize our detection process by minimizing long-term losses. Our approach involves dividing the system's operational timeline into distinct phases, each characterized by stable dynamics, and we focus on minimizing the error incurred during transitions between these phases.

We have carried out detailed chemical evolution modelling of three small galaxies, specifically Antlia, Segue 1, and Draco, to understand their past development. By combining precise measurements of individual element abundances with recent data on the ages of their stellar populations, we have been able to refine our models of their chemical evolution. Our analysis reveals that these galaxies experienced rapid, short-lived bursts of star formation early on, followed by a decline in activity. The star formation efficiency in these galaxies was found to be relatively low, with values of 0.003-0.005 for Draco and a maximum of 0.01 for Antlia. The metal content of these galaxies, however, showed a more diverse range, with Draco and Antlia exhibiting a maximum metal content of 0.15 and 0.1 respectively, while a subset of Draco's population exhibited a maximum metal content of 0.05. The models also indicate that the abundance patterns of these galaxies are consistent with a scenario in which their star formation was triggered by internal processes, rather than external factors.

We establish a category of graded $E$-spectra for a profinite group $G$, denoted as $\mathrm{Sp}_*^{\bullet,G}$, which is the full subcategory of $\mathrm{Sp}_*^{\bullet,\hat{G}}$ consisting of spectra with trivial actions by the topological fundamental group $\hat{G}$ of the profinite space. This allows us to define a homotopy orbit spectrum for any graded $E$-spectrum, which in turn enables the application of classical Bökstedt-Pagans localization techniques to compute $\mathrm{Sp}_*^{\bullet,G}$ through iterated Bökstedt-Pagans spectral sequences.

A major challenge in developing machine learning models for visually complex business documents is the high expense associated with data labeling. Our proposal, a two-step process, significantly reduces this cost by leveraging pre-trained image and language models. Initially, an image-based model generates field definitions and content within each business document field. Subsequently, a labeling interface allows annotators to correct any inaccuracies in the automatically created labels. Our method was tested on 100 annotations across three distinct business document types: insurance policies, bank statements, and invoices. The results showed that our approach requires just 10 annotations to achieve comparable accuracy to models trained with full, manually created labels, a 10-fold reduction in expense.

The EuS/InAs interface has garnered significant interest due to its potential to exhibit a giant magnetic semiconductor property in conjunction with a topological superconductor. A detailed investigation of the electronic structure at this interface was conducted using a combination of first-principles calculations and experimental X-ray photoemission spectroscopy. A key finding is that the InAs substrate induces band bending within the EuS layer, with a magnitude of approximately 0.3 eV. Furthermore, the study identified interface states situated within the InAs band gap, exhibiting characteristics of a magnetic origin. These interface states demonstrate a significant spin polarization of around 60%, with their position being tunable through the application of light.

A comprehensive classification system for subsets of Baire space, categorized by their Badge classes, has been introduced. Although the total number of distinct Badge classes is infinite and uncountable, an effective way to differentiate them has been established. We provide an algorithm capable of determining, for any two indices, whether the corresponding sets are equivalent under the Badge relation.

Deep neural networks have achieved remarkable success in various machine learning tasks, but their high computational and memory requirements make them impractical for deployment on resource-constrained devices. To address this issue, we have developed ClickTrain, an innovative neural network pruning approach that can significantly reduce the computational and memory costs of DL models while maintaining their accuracy. ClickTrain enables efficient training of compressed DL models by predicting precise pruning points for redundant operations within a model, thereby eliminating the need for post-training optimization. Our approach outperforms existing solutions by achieving a model compression rate of up to 3.2x while only marginally affecting accuracy, resulting in a 2.1x speedup and a 1.8x reduction in memory usage when deployed on edge devices.

This study examines the properties of specific modal logics derived from noncommutative lattices by incorporating $\Box$ and $\Diamond$ into the distributive full Lambek calculus with modal operators. A key aspect of this investigation involves demonstrating that a semantic model based on ordered pairs of modal noncommutative po-groups provides a sound and complete framework for the defined modal logics.

The merging of neutron stars and black holes is a significant area of study in astronomy, as it allows scientists to observe the behavior of these celestial objects. By using gravitational waves, researchers can gain insight into previously unobservable aspects of these objects, such as their masses and the event horizons of black holes. Although traditional methods for analyzing these waves have limitations, new techniques based on machine learning offer promising alternatives. A recent study aimed to develop a deep learning-based method for analyzing neutron star-black hole mergers, using simulated gravitational wave data from the SpyKE simulation framework. The results showed that a convolutional neural network could accurately detect and classify these mergers, achieving high levels of precision and recall. The study found that the proposed method outperformed traditional template-matching methods, particularly in cases of low signal-to-noise ratio. Furthermore, the study found that the deep learning-based method was more efficient, requiring significantly less computational resources than template-matching methods. Overall, the results suggest that deep learning-based methods have the potential to play a significant role in the future of gravitational wave astronomy, providing new ways to analyze these important phenomena.

A comprehensive study of the newly discovered exoplanetary system TOI-5542 is presented. Utilizing data from the TESS mission, we identified and analyzed 13 candidate transits, with the most promising being the one occurring on day 100.18, which exhibits a period of 1.21 days. By incorporating radial velocity measurements from the Keck and Magellan telescopes, we confirmed the existence of the candidate exoplanet and named it TOI-5542b. This exoplanet has a mass of 1.11 MJ and a radius of 1.22 RJ, indicating that it is an old, warm Jupiter. Notably, TOI-5542b is characterized by its extremely low host star metallicity of -1.24 dex, which is consistent with the host star's age of approximately 10 billion years. TOI-5542b is also one of the few known exoplanets with a significant eccentricity of 0.31, which suggests that it may be subject to gravitational interactions with other bodies in the system. TOI-5542b is also a member of a rare class of exoplanets known as "warm Jupiters," which are characterized by their relatively low orbital inclinations and temperatures. We investigate an online algorithm for constrained Markov decision processes, 
exemplifying Markov decision processes with limited resources such as energy 
or memory. Our approach leverages online convex optimization under a coupling 
framework to address the trade-off between system performance and constraint 
adherence. We analyze the algorithm's performance using a novel framework that 
integrates online control and constrained convex optimization, yielding a 
performance guarantee that explicitly shows how the tuning parameter influences 
the system's stability and constraint violation.

A novel, comprehensive system for recognizing handwritten mathematical symbols offline has been developed, leveraging a wide range of diverse characters. The system utilizes a combination of feature extraction techniques and classification algorithms, specifically designed to handle complex mathematical symbols consisting of multiple strokes. Additionally, the system incorporates a dataset of mathematical symbols annotated with corresponding ground truth information, facilitating efficient training and testing. The results demonstrate the system's exceptional recognition accuracy, surpassing existing state-of-the-art methods.

We explore the connection between sheaf cohomology and supercohomology in the context of supermanifolds, drawing an analogy with Hilbert series of K\"ahler spaces. This approach utilizes BPS states in supersymmetric quantum mechanics, which correspond to supercohomology classes. The linear sigma model serves as a key example, and its string theory dual, described by a D-brane, provides insight into the computational method for Hilbert series via the partition function of supersymmetric quantum mechanics. We demonstrate that the growth rate of the Hilbert series can be calculated from the partition function's pole order and can also be determined through a geometric interpretation based on the fixed point manifolds of the scalar fields under a U(1) action.

The contact process is an essential model for describing disease spread, and its behavior changes significantly depending on the contact structure.  In many real-world scenarios, network interactions are non-random, and the variability of the contact structure can greatly impact the model's outcome.  This study examines the contact process within different network frameworks, focusing on the differences between heterogeneity and clustering effects.  We investigate how the disease variability is affected by a general class of network variations, using both theoretical analysis and computer simulations.  Our results demonstrate that node degree variations can increase disease fluctuation, and a theoretical model accurately predicts this behavior for random networks with given degree distributions.  However, this prediction does not hold for network variations that promote local clustering, and in these cases, the model exhibits reduced disease variability.  This study provides a comprehensive understanding of the relationship between network structure and disease spread, and our findings have implications for the analysis of disease outbreaks in complex contact structures.

Actor-Critic reinforcement learning algorithms have been widely used in robotics and gaming due to their effectiveness in solving Markov decision processes. However, these methods can be susceptible to local optima and struggle with complex problems. A promising solution lies in employing Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) to generate more informed policy updates. HMC, a well-established method in Bayesian statistics, can be used to create a stochastic gradient descent process that samples from a target distribution. By leveraging HMC to update the actor, we can improve the exploration of the policy's parameter space. Our approach, known as \textit{Hamiltonian Monte Carlo Method for Reinforcement Learning (HMC4RL)}, integrates HMC into actor-critic reinforcement learning to achieve better performance. Experimental results on multiple benchmark tasks demonstrate the superiority of our method, showing improved sample efficiency and final reward compared to existing actor-critic baselines.

A novel approach to addressing the long-standing twin prime conjecture is presented, leveraging a straightforward combinatorial argument that relies on a basic principle of inclusion-exclusion. This combinatorial method is initially applied to demonstrate Euler's product formula for the zeta function and then used to establish a formula for counting primes within a given interval. This established formula serves as a foundational step towards a potential proof of the strong Goldbach conjecture and the long conjecture, ultimately providing a pathway to the twin prime conjecture.

Mobile robots rely on accurate navigation data to operate effectively, but real-world sonar readings are often distorted by noise and anomalies. These distortions can cause a robot to misinterpret its surroundings, hindering its ability to navigate safely. To address this issue, we've developed a real-time sonar fusion algorithm that cleans up raw sonar data, removing noise and correcting distortions. This technique uses a real-time navigation system to create a layered map of the environment, allowing the robot to navigate in real-time. By comparing the robot's current sonar data to the existing map, we can identify and remove distortions, creating a clear and accurate picture of the environment. This approach has been tested on a mobile robot in a real-world setting, and we've found that it significantly improves the robot's navigation capabilities.

Nereid, a retrograde orbiting satellite of Neptune, is a well-preserved relic from the early solar system's formation. Its composition, consisting of water ice and other materials, can be analyzed through its reflectance spectrum. By comparing Nereid's spectrum to that of laboratory water ice mixtures, researchers found that Nereid's surface composition is similar to a mixture of 50% water ice and 50% dark material, with a 50/50 ratio. This complex mixture is consistent with the presence of hydrated silicates and other dark materials. The findings suggest that Nereid's surface has undergone minimal space weathering and that its composition is consistent with a body that formed through the accretion of icy planetesimals.

Let $T_n(\mathbb{F})$ be the set of lower triangular matrices of size $n \times n$ with entries from a finite field $\mathbb{F}$ of size $q$. In our research, we explore affine and projective planes constructed from these matrices, denoted as $\mathcal{A}_n(\mathbb{F})$ and $\mathcal{P}_n(\mathbb{F})$. We prove that these constructed planes satisfy the line-Lazebskii Skolem theorem when $n$ is an odd number, and also provide a counterexample for a specific case where this construction fails for even $n$.

In a 1986 paper in J. Symbolic Logic, Pawlikowski demonstrated that under the condition of being Tukey-order greater than the order of the ideal of null sets with Lebesgue measure, a certain type of non-principal ultrafilter would result in a contradiction with a well-known independence result. This became a significant unsolved problem until a 2019 paper by Blass and others proved that a specific condition related to Tukey-order and three types of linear orderings can imply the same condition related to the above-mentioned ultrafilter. This made it possible to establish relationships between certain linear orderings and another type of independence result.

A new method for Bayesian policy optimization under uncertainty is developed, creating a value function that balances the trade-off between optimality and safety by being greater than or equal to the optimal value function and being maximized when the degree of pessimism increases. It is proven that any action chosen to maximize this function ensures that the system remains stable and provides a bound on the difference between the value of this policy and the optimal policy, which decreases exponentially as sample size grows. Numerical experiments show that this method performs well in a variety of settings and its properties can be applied in both offline and online scenarios.

Dualities between categories of graded modules over endomorphism rings of complexes of graded injectives are investigated, with a focus on the properties of the underlying homological algebra. The study generalizes previous work by Christensen, Hoshino, and Takahashi to a broader class of rings, specifically those with finite projective dimension. The results are then utilized to approximate derived functors and compute invariants such as local cohomology and F-contramodules for these rings.
