In a flat band superconductor, the phase coherence of its ground state is remarkably robust, even in the absence of multiple Cooper pairs. Our research reveals that superconducting states emerging from a specific type of flat band, characterized by its topological properties, exhibit an enhanced stability. The stability of these states is a result of the unique correlation between electrons within a single band, which contrasts with the electron pairing process observed in conventional superconductors. Our findings are supported by both analytical and computational analyses, including a demonstration that the superconducting gap is closed when interlayer interactions are removed. The robustness of these states also extends to the presence of magnetic impurities, which fail to suppress the gap when coupled through spin-flip interactions. Our research has implications for the study of superconductivity in materials with frustrated interactions and highly correlated electrons.

The Gaussian distribution is uniquely characterized by a distribution function on a one-dimensional locally compact abelian group with the property that for any given distribution, there exists a non-zero constant, such that the convolution of the distribution with itself is less than or equal to the sum of the distribution at any two points, minus a non-zero constant. This is in line with a broader theorem by Polya, which applies to all non-empty, open intervals within the real numbers. A similar, but more specific, result was previously established for the torus by Diaconis and Goldberger. A dimension one condition for the applicability of this characterizing result has now been proved for all locally compact abelian groups.

Presence-absence data is frequently encountered in ecological research and is typically characterized by sparse patterns. Traditional clustering methods struggle to effectively analyze such data due to its inherent sparsity. A new clustering approach has been developed to overcome these limitations, and in this research, it is compared to existing methods through both simulated and real-world ecological datasets.

This research introduces an innovative and streamlined salient object detection approach that works with both RGB and RGB-D inputs, resulting in more accurate outcomes. A combination of a color-based module and an orientation-invariant structure enables this method to process RGB inputs effectively. Additionally, depth information is integrated through a depth-aware module to further enhance its performance on RGB-D inputs. A series of progressive connections is employed to refine the output, which is then enhanced by a de-normalization technique using background information. Extensive experiments conducted on a variety of datasets demonstrate the method's superior performance compared to existing techniques, particularly in the areas of RGB and RGB-D inputs.

The UM-IU@LING system for offensive tweet detection at offensiveness.net-2019 Task 6 employed a two-part strategy to classify tweets as offensive or not. First, a BERT model was fine-tuned to generate intermediate representations, which were then used by a linear Support Vector Machine classifier to make a preliminary classification. In cases where the BERT-SVM model expressed uncertainty, human reviewers were consulted to determine the tweet's offensiveness. This system achieved a strong F1 score of 0.7832 in the offensiveness classification task, placing it in a top 10 position, and also demonstrated effectiveness in distinguishing between different types of offensiveness.

A number is considered a palindrome if its binary representation reads the same forwards and backwards. This study examines the best possible results for a palindrome quotient when dividing a palindromic number by one of its components, with a similar analysis for numbers that are palindromes in reverse.

Computed tomography (CT) is a widely used medical imaging technique that uses X-rays to create detailed images of the human body. However, standard polyenergetic CT reconstruction methods have limitations in accurately identifying certain materials, such as those that are mixed or have varying energy levels. To overcome these limitations, a new approach has been developed that combines a convex optimization method with a Bregman iteration technique to simultaneously reconstruct images, remove noise from detectors, and identify materials. The method relies on a specially designed objective function that takes into account images at different energy levels and uses a fixed matrix to represent the X-ray paths. The approach has been successfully tested on synthetic data and shows promise in improving material identification accuracy.

Handwritten text recognition is a crucial task in various applications, but it's particularly challenging due to handwriting diversity. Although deep learning methods have achieved significant success, they require substantial amounts of data, which is often impractical to obtain for handwritten text. To overcome this limitation, we have developed a novel data augmentation approach that generates synthetic handwriting samples from scratch using a single example per character class. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in significantly improving the recognition performance of a RNN-T based handwritten text recognition system when trained with limited data.

Within the ab initio no-core shell model framework, we have computed the low-lying properties of Tin isotopes ranging from 104 to 126, achieving convergence for all ground and excited states. Our calculations encompass a wide range of nuclear regions, including a doubly-magic nucleus at 126Sn, as well as two deformed isotopes, 110Sn and 112Sn, and a tin isotope chain featuring a transition from a quadrupole vibrator to a well-deformed rotor. By integrating multiple theoretical approaches, we have successfully converged the ab initio no-core shell model to a novel, more comprehensive method. Our calculations include a realistically interacting Hamiltonian, a large number of configurations, and a vast number of basis states, thereby achieving a fully converged, ab initio no-core shell model.

In solid-state physics, there's a growing interest in topological phenomena, particularly those that are intrinsic to one-dimensional systems, such as the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model. To better understand this model, we'll start by examining its Hamiltonian and performing a mean-field analysis to obtain an effective Hamiltonian in terms of electron creation and annihilation operators. By performing a $k$-space transformation, we can derive the effective $k$-space Hamiltonian and its corresponding eigenvalue problem. The resulting energy spectrum will be compared to that of the nearest neighbor tight-binding model, and the topological properties of the SSH model will be investigated by calculating the energy bands and wave functions. The concept of the Chern number will be introduced, and its application to the SSH model will be demonstrated. The results of this analysis will provide a deeper understanding of the topological phenomena observed in the SSH model, and may serve as a foundation for exploring other one-dimensional topological models.

This study examines the compactness of composition operators within Bergman spaces associated with certain bounded, convex domains in complex n-dimensional space containing non-trivial analytic circles in the boundary. Consequently, this characterizes compactness of the composition operator with a continuous symbol mapping to the same Bergman space space, based on the symbol's behavior at the boundary.
